title: NOAA ERSSTv6 has an undocumented warm step of +0.05-0.07 C in 2016-2017 (60S-60N) that ERSSTv5 lacks; it makes 2019 falsely warmer than 2016 and inflates ERSSTv6 warming acceleration
abstract: Question: ERSSTv6 (NOAA, 2025) replaces the EOT interpolation of ERSSTv5 with a neural network and adds new quality control, with the same in situ data. Does it have step artifacts, and what do they change? Approach: at 60S-60N, 1982-2025, on the 29,976-point mask of the campaign's blind joint homogenisation (sci:sha256:d9bdf1f8), we used four designs: the published joint search with ERSSTv6 added or in place of ERSSTv5; a single-series search of ERSSTv6 minus a consensus of homogenised products made without ERSSTv6; 36-month window tests against 13 product series; and in situ HadSST4.2 and Argo references. Results: the reproduced joint search gives the published 23 steps. All designs find a warm ERSSTv6 step in 2016-2017: +0.066 +/- 0.005 C in 2017-01 in the joint search, and +0.021 C (2016-01) plus +0.045 C (2017-07) against the consensus. Against HadSST4.2 the 2017 step is +0.057 +/- 0.006 C in ERSSTv6 and +0.014 C in ERSSTv5; the Argo contrast is +0.044 C. The step is equal in well-sampled and partly sampled boxes, so it is not an infilling artifact. A -0.03 C step in 2020-09 (common to both ERSST versions) and a 2023 fall partly reverse it. Published ERSSTv6 makes 2019 0.046 C warmer than 2016 (other products -0.019 to +0.003 C; corrected v6 -0.021 to +0.001 C), so its 2019 record is an artifact. Its warming acceleration c = 0.0385 K per decade^2 is the largest of eight products and falls to 0.023 after correction; its 2023/24 jump falls from 0.232 to 0.200 C. Limitations: the cause is not proven (the date is near a documented 2017 change of the ERSST data-ingest stream); shared errors are invisible; the consensus trend itself changes by 0.01 C per decade when ERSSTv6 replaces ERSSTv5.
